```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(base)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(xtable)
library(stargazer)
library(plm)
library(sjPlot)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
```

#Data Loading and Recoding
```{r}
ess_ches = read.csv(here::here("data", "ess_ches.csv"))
ches = read.csv(here::here("data", "ches1419.csv"))

ess_ches$Christian = ifelse(ess_ches$religion == 1, 1, 0)
ess_ches$Muslim = ifelse(ess_ches$religion == 2, 1, 0)

ess_ches$imatt = NA
ess_ches$imatt = 1/3*(ess_ches$imbgeco + ess_ches$imueclt + ess_ches$imwbcnt)

ess_ches$immpol = NA
ess_ches$immpol = 1/3*(ess_ches$impol1 + ess_ches$impol2 + ess_ches$impol3)
```

#Descriptive Statistics
##Sample (Appendix A: Table A1)
```{r}
sample = as.data.frame.matrix(table(ess_ches$country, ess_ches$status))
sample$total = rowSums(sample)

sample = sample %>%
  mutate(
    native_pct  = round(native / total * 100, 2),
    first_pct   = round(first / total * 100, 2),
    second_pct  = round(second / total * 100, 2),
    total_pct   = 100
  )

sample_fmt <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    Native      = paste0(format(native, big.mark=","), " (", native_pct, ")"),
    FirstGen    = paste0(format(first, big.mark=","), " (", first_pct, ")"),
    SecondGen   = paste0(format(second, big.mark=","), " (", second_pct, ")"),
    TotalSample = paste0(format(total, big.mark=","), " (", total_pct, ")")
  ) %>%
  select(Native, FirstGen, SecondGen, TotalSample)

status_xtable = xtable(sample_fmt, caption = "Immigrant Status by Country")
print(status_xtable, include.rownames = TRUE, sanitize.rownames.function = identity,
      file = here::here("Figures", "Table A1_sample_summary.tex"))
```

## Political Party Positions on Immigration Policy
```{r}
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(sf)
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
Europe <- world[which(world$continent == "Europe"),]
world_map = map_data("world") %>% 
  filter(! long > 180)
#table(world_map$region)
```

```{r}
#this will create Europe 2 which will be used for Figure A1 (without weight)
average_by_country <- ches %>%
  filter(year == 2019) %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_immigrate_policy = mean(immigrate_policy, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(mean_immigrate_policy)

#this will create Europe 4
average_by_country3 <- ess_ches %>%# Subset the data
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_immigrate_policy2 = mean(immigrate_policy, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(mean_immigrate_policy2)

print(average_by_country3)

Europe$iso_a2_eh
average_by_country$iso_a2_eh <- average_by_country$country
average_by_country$mean_immigrate_policy

average_by_country3$country
average_by_country3$iso_a2_eh <- average_by_country3$country
average_by_country3$mean_immigrate_policy
average_by_country3$region <- c("Portugal","Finland","Ireland","Estonia","Germany", "Spain", "UK", "Belgium","Lithuania","France","Netherlands","Sweden", "Denmark","Slovenia","Cyprus","Croatia","Italy","Belgium","Poland", "Austria","Czech Republic", "Hungary","Slovakia")

Europe2 <- left_join(Europe, average_by_country, by="iso_a2_eh")
Europe4 <- left_join(Europe, average_by_country3, by="iso_a2_eh")

Europe2$mean_immigrate_policy_r <-round(Europe2$mean_immigrate_policy,2)
Europe4$mean_immigrate_policy_r <-round(Europe4$mean_immigrate_policy,2)
```


#Figure 1: Average Immigration Policy Position (Map)
For Figure 1, we weighted the average party positions on immigration policy by their vote share (multiplying the average policy position by the party's vote share)
```{r}
ggplot(Europe4) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill=mean_immigrate_policy2)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-20,35), ylim = c(35,72), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="lightblue",high="darkblue",
                      na.value="gray95")+
  geom_sf_label(aes(label=mean_immigrate_policy_r),fill = "white", 
                 size=3) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        text=element_text(size=13)) 

ggsave(here::here("Figures", "Figure 1_map.png"), width=10,height=7)
```


#Figure A1
Figure A1 is an average immigration policy positions among political parties by country without any weight.
```{r}
ggplot(Europe2) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill=mean_immigrate_policy)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-20,35), ylim = c(35,72), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="#d1ffbd",high="darkgreen", 
                      breaks=c(4,5,6,7), 
                      labels=c("4 anti-immigration","5","6","7 pro-immigration"),
                      name="",
                      na.value="gray95")+
  geom_sf_label(aes(label=mean_immigrate_policy_r),fill = "white", 
                 size=3) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right",legend.key.height = unit(.8, "cm"),
        text=element_text(size=13)) 

ggsave(here::here("Figures", "Figure A1_map.png"), width=10,height=7)
```


#Appendix C: Party Categorization (Table A2)
```{r}
# Step 1: Aggregate the data to get the mean of immigrate_policy for each party in each country
party_aggregated = ess_ches %>%
  group_by(country, party) %>%
  summarise(immigrate_policy = mean(immigrate_policy, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Create a new column that combines party names with their values
party_aggregated = party_aggregated %>%
  mutate(party_value = paste0(party, " (", round(immigrate_policy, 2), ")"))

# Step 3: Group by country
country_party_table = party_aggregated %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(parties = paste(party_value, collapse = ", ")) %>%
  ungroup()

# results
print(country_party_table)
latex2 = xtable(country_party_table)
```

##Individual-Level Variables

#Table 1: Average Political Attitudes by Country
```{r}
fmt = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", format(round(x,2), nsmall = 2))
average_all = ess_ches %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    immpol_all = mean(immpol, na.rm = T),
    imatt_all = mean(imatt, na.rm = T),
    lrscale_all = mean(lrscale, na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

average_first = ess_ches %>%
  filter(status == "first") %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    immpol_first = mean(immpol, na.rm = T),
    imatt_first = mean(imatt, na.rm = T),
    lrscale_first = mean(lrscale, na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

average_country = average_all %>%
  left_join(average_first, by = "country") %>%
  mutate(
    `Average Attitudes Towards Policy`     = paste0(fmt(immpol_all),  " (", fmt(immpol_first),  ")"),
    `Average Attitudes Towards Immigrants` = paste0(fmt(imatt_all),   " (", fmt(imatt_first),   ")"),
    `Average Political Ideology`           = paste0(fmt(lrscale_all), " (", fmt(lrscale_first), ")")
  ) %>%
  select(
    Country = country,
    `Average Attitudes Towards Policy`,
    `Average Attitudes Towards Immigrants`,
    `Average Political Ideology`
  )

overall_all = ess_ches %>%
  summarise(
    immpol_all  = mean(immpol, na.rm = TRUE),
    imatt_all   = mean(imatt,  na.rm = TRUE),
    lrscale_all = mean(lrscale, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

overall_first = ess_ches %>%
  filter(status == "first") %>%
  summarise(
    immpol_first  = mean(immpol, na.rm = TRUE),
    imatt_first   = mean(imatt,  na.rm = TRUE),
    lrscale_first = mean(lrscale, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

overall_row = tibble(
  Country = "Overall",
  `Average Attitudes Towards Policy`     = paste0(fmt(overall_all$immpol_all),  " (", fmt(overall_first$immpol_first),  ")"),
  `Average Attitudes Towards Immigrants` = paste0(fmt(overall_all$imatt_all),   " (", fmt(overall_first$imatt_first),   ")"),
  `Average Political Ideology`           = paste0(fmt(overall_all$lrscale_all), " (", fmt(overall_first$lrscale_first), ")")
)

avg_table = bind_rows(avg_by_country, overall_row)
table1 = xtable(avg_table, caption = "Average Political Attitudes by Country")
print(table1, include.rownames = TRUE, sanitize.rownames.function = identity,
      file = here::here("Figures", "Table 1_Summary.tex"))

```


#Figure 2: Distributions of Individual Preferences Across Immigration Status
```{r}
subplot1 = ggplot(ess_ches) + 
  geom_density(aes(imatt, fill=status),alpha=0.5) + 
  labs(x="Immigrant attitude", y="") +
  theme_bw()+  theme(text=element_text(size=13))

subplot2 = ggplot(ess_ches) + 
  geom_density(aes(immpol, fill=status),alpha=0.5,adjust=1.5) + 
  labs(x="Immigration policy attitude", y="") +
  theme_bw()+ theme(text=element_text(size=13))

subplot3 = ggplot(ess_ches, aes(group=status)) + 
  geom_density(aes(lrscale, fill=status),alpha=0.5,adjust=1.5) + 
  labs(x="Left-right scale", y="Density") +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels=c("Native","First","Second"), name="Status")+
  theme_bw() + theme(text=element_text(size=13))


figure2 = ggarrange(subplot3,subplot1, subplot2, 
                        ncol=3, common.legend = T, legend="bottom")

ggsave(here::here("Figures", "Figure 2.png"), width=12,height=4)
```

#Factor Analysis (Table A3)
```{r}
#six variables for outcome variables #factor analysis
vars = ess_ches[, c("imbgeco", "imueclt", "imwbcnt", "impol1", "impol2", "impol3")]
fa_result = factanal(vars, factors = 2, rotation = "varimax", scores = "regression")
print(fa_result, digits = 3, cutoff = 0.3)  

sink(here::here("Figures", "Table A3_FA.tex"))
print(fa_result, digits = 3, cutoff = 0.3)
sink()
```

```{r}
summary(ess_ches$immigrate_policy)
# Plotting histogram with y-axis as proportions
hist(ess_ches$immigrate_policy, freq = FALSE, 
     main = "Party's Position on Immigration Policy",
     xlab = "0 = strongly liberal, 10 = strongly restrictive", ylab = "Proportion")

# Calculate the mean of ess_ches$immigrate_policy
mean_value <- mean(ess_ches$immigrate_policy, na.rm = TRUE)

# Add a vertical line for the mean
abline(v = mean_value, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

# Add text above the vertical line for the mean value
text(mean_value, 0.1, labels = paste("Mean =", round(mean_value, 2)), pos = 4, col = "red")
```
